rationale: P identifies braking initiation and execution, which are themselves the system behaviours required to evaluate prevention of omitted braking maneuvers. SG-1 and FR-7 establish this focus, while FR-7.1 establishes the relationship between obstacle detection and braking initiation. Detection is expressed as a triggering condition, not as an expansion into sensing or processing mechanisms. The declared operational scope matches H-1.
determining_elements: “Whether braking is initiated and performed” directly characterises the occurrence or omission of the required braking maneuver.
“When an obstacle is detected in time” provides the context for the braking response; P does not incorporate detection processing or its latency as a separate phenomenon.
The straight-ahead, single-lane-road scenario at 50 km/h in good weather, with a pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead, is explicitly supported by H-1.
No internal observation, computation, communication, or control mechanisms are added to the braking behaviour being characterised.
